newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's QTC saves A$95.5 mln in 1995/96.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's QTC saves A$95.5 mln in 1995/96.

text.p: Queensland Treasury Corp (QTC) said on Thursday that lower borrowings and interest rate management costs prodcued savings of A$95.5 million in 1995/96.

Releasing QTC's annual report, Chairman Sir Leo Hielscher said 1995/96 had been a highly successful year with QTC maintaining the highest performance levels of Australian semi-government central borrowing agencies and embarking on a major new business direction.
QTC borrows on behalf of major Queensland state government agencies, which includes local governments, electricity bodies and port authorities.
QTC's savings since its inception in 1988 now total A$621.3 million and since 1991 its borrowing client base had grown to 165 from 81 with onlendings totalling A$13.5 billion, the annual report said.
Hielscher said that through an enhanced emphasis on customer service, which had involved significant restructuring, QTC aimed to provide even better outcomes for its public sector customers.

"This fundamental shift in service provision has proved extremely valuable in assisting customers to adapt to the requirements of the National Competition Policy, commercialisation and corporatisation of public sector business
and deregulation in the marketplace," he said.

QTC has appointed two new Board members in 1996, Vince O'Rourke, Chief Executive of Queensland Rail, and Richard Anderson, Senior Partner of Coopers & Lybrand, to strengthen representation from outside professionals and of customers serviced by the corporation.

"During the year, QTC expanded its range of customer debt pools by establishing five new credit foncier based pools and more importantly, a facility which allows customers to put in place funding facilities specifically structured to meet individual requirements," Hielscher said.

"QTC also maintained its diverse domestic and international funding base to ensure that customers continue to have access to a world-class portfolio of funding and risk management instruments," he added.
